name: notalune
description: Read sheet music: notes drawn on a staff, a note-reading drill on an on-screen piano, and a metronome.

interface.longDescription:
Notalune helps you read sheet music, right in the conversation.

Practise notes: a row of notes appears on a properly engraved staff, as in a piece, and you tap each one on an on-screen piano keyboard, so no real piano is needed (or switch to one note at a time). Rounds of 24 notes, with a progress bar, end with stars and the notes to watch, and you can ask ChatGPT about the ones you missed. Thirty-three chapters run from middle C through ledger lines, the bass clef, both hands, scales and broken chords in both clefs, and key signatures up to three sharps or flats, or ChatGPT can set up a drill for the range and key of the piece you are learning.

Show notes: ask what a note, scale, interval or chord looks like on the staff or where it is on the piano, and Notalune draws it with the names and marks the keys.

Metronome: Notalune's wooden mechanical metronome, from 40 to 208 beats per minute, 2 to 4 beats per bar with a bell. Tap the pendulum or the knob to start, drag the weight or turn the knob to set the tempo.

Note names in the system you read: letters (C D E), the German and Czech H-system, solfège (Do Re Mi) or Japanese ドレミ, in seven languages. Notalune's server stores nothing: what you play stays in the panel.

Limits: it does not read rhythm, play whole pieces or listen to your instrument inside ChatGPT. The Notalune app for iPhone and iPad, which writes the note names onto your own printed sheet music, is a separate product.
capabilities: Note-reading drill on an on-screen piano keyboard
Draw notes, scales, intervals and chords on the staff
Wooden mechanical metronome from 40 to 208 BPM
defaultPrompt: Quiz me on the notes of the bass clef.
Show me the D major scale on the staff.

positive.description: Bass clef practice from a learner's request
positive.prompt: I'm learning piano and keep forgetting the bass clef notes. Can you help me practise?
positive.expected_behavior: A drill opens on a bass staff (a bass-clef chapter such as 8 or 9) with a row of notes. Tapping the matching key on the on-screen keyboard turns the note green and moves on to the next note in the row; a wrong key turns it red. 'One by one' switches to a single note at a time. After 24 notes the panel shows 0 to 3 stars, how many were right first time and the notes to watch.

positive.description: A chord drawn on the staff
positive.prompt: What does a C major chord look like on the staff?
positive.expected_behavior: A treble staff with C4, E4 and G4 stacked as one chord with no key signature, each with its name, and the three keys marked on the keyboard. Play sounds the chord on a piano.

positive.description: A scale in another naming system
positive.prompt: Show me the G major scale in the treble clef with solfège names.
positive.expected_behavior: G major from G4 to G5 with F♯ (as a key signature or an accidental), labelled Sol La Si Do Re Mi Fa♯ Sol with octave numbers, and the keys marked.

positive.description: A drill for the notes of a piece
positive.prompt: I'm learning the opening of Für Elise. Can I practise reading its notes?
positive.expected_behavior: A treble-clef drill on the opening's own notes in order (E5 D♯5 E5 D♯5 E5 B4 D5 C5 A4 …, the only accidental D♯ and later G♯), titled after the piece, read row by row. Rounds of 24 notes as in the first case.

positive.description: A metronome at a tempo and metre
positive.prompt: Give me a metronome at 72 BPM in 3/4.
positive.expected_behavior: The wooden metronome opens at 72 BPM (Adagio) with 3 beats per bar selected. Tapping the knob starts it ticking with a bell once per bar and the pendulum swinging; tapping again stops it. Turning the knob or dragging the weight changes the tempo.

negative.prompt: Transcribe this recording into sheet music for me.

negative.description: General music history needs no tool

negative.prompt: Buy me a digital piano under 500 dollars.

review.commerce_description: The plugin sells nothing and takes no payments.

publication.release_notes: First release: a note-reading drill on an on-screen piano, notes drawn on the staff, and Notalune's wooden metronome.
